title: Book a counselling session (Student Wellbeing & Counselling)
summary: Free, confidential individual counselling for full-time and part-time students, in person or online. Not for emergencies: the team replies within 3 working days.
steps: Log in to the Kaplan360 app.
Tap the "Academic" icon in the bottom navigation bar.
Open the "Counselling" tab.
Tap "+ New" (bottom right) and fill in the Counselling Request Form.
Answer all questions and tap "Submit". The counselling team will contact you within 3 working days.
notes: Counsellors do not diagnose or prescribe medication. Confidential, except where there is an imminent threat to life or safety.
contact: Student Wellbeing & Counselling, via the Kaplan360 app

title: Apply for leave when you miss class (Leave of Absence)
summary: Apply for leave in the Kaplan360 app at least 1 working day before class, or within 3 working days after an emergency. Maximum 3 days per application.
steps: Open the Kaplan360 app.
Go to the leave application section (SAMPLE: exact menu path not yet verified).
Choose your leave dates and reason.
Upload supporting documents (e.g. MC, death notice, employer letter, NS letter). If leaving Singapore, also upload your flight itinerary or boarding pass.
Submit. Student Services approves or rejects within 5 working days.
notes: Valid grounds: illness (MC from a Singapore-registered doctor, TCM practitioner, dentist or hospital), compassionate (immediate family, up to 3 working days), accident, National Service, work commitment, legal commitment. NOT accepted: holidays planned after the programme started, oversleeping, misreading the timetable, poor network. Need more than 3 days? Consider deferment instead.
contact: Your programme's Student Services team (see the Student Services contacts entry)

title: How attendance works (QR scanning and minimum rates)
summary: Scan the class QR code twice: within 15 minutes of the start, and again after class ends. Student's Pass holders need 90% monthly attendance; everyone else needs 75%.
steps: Scan the QR code shown in class within 15 minutes of the start (later counts as late).
Scan again after the class ends (missing it counts as leaving early).
If the QR code won't scan, tell your lecturer so they can mark you manually.
Check your real-time attendance rate in the Kaplan360 app.
notes: Online classes: attendance is based on logging in and taking part. Asynchronous lessons: based on accessing materials in the LMS. Student's Pass holders below 90% are reported to ICA; 7 consecutive days absent can lead to Student's Pass cancellation.
contact: Your lecturer (for scanning issues) or Student Services

title: Find your classes, timetable and classroom
summary: Your personalised timetable and assigned classrooms are in the Kaplan360 app.
steps: Open the Kaplan360 app and log in.
Open your timetable / study plan (SAMPLE: exact menu path not yet verified).
Tap a class to see its time and assigned classroom.
Check which campus the room is at (Wilkie Edge, Odeon 331 or Odeon 333).
notes: Online classes and materials are on your LMS (see the LMS entry). Don't have Kaplan360 login details yet? See the Kaplan360 login entry.

title: Get access to the Kaplan360 app
summary: Kaplan360 login details are sent to you after your programme officially starts. Kaplan360 lets you check classrooms, notifications, attendance, apply for leave, complete the onboarding checklist and update contact details.
steps: Download Kaplan360 from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.
Log in with the credentials Kaplan sends you after your programme starts.
Haven't received them, or locked out? Contact your Student Services team.
notes: Access to Kaplan360 and the LMS is suspended if you have outstanding fees (Bad Financial Standing).

title: Access the LMS (study guides, assignments, results)
summary: Study guides, assignment submission, exam rules and final grades are on the eLearn Learning Management System (LMS). University partner programmes may also use the university's own portal.
steps: Go to the eLearn LMS login page (SAMPLE: URL not yet verified).
Log in with your student account.
Open your module to find the study guide and assignment submission page.
Submit assignments before the deadline. The submission portal only opens within the stated dates.
notes: Uploading the correct file is your responsibility. Murdoch students' enrolled units also appear in the Murdoch University student portal.

title: Check exam results
summary: Final grades are released on the LMS within 30 calendar days after the exam. Phone and walk-in grade enquiries are not entertained.
steps: Log in to the LMS about 30 days after your exam.
Open your module to view the final grade.
Disagree with a result? See the academic appeal entry. You have 7 working days.
notes: For academic records or certificate verification after graduating, email academicrecords.sg@kaplan.com.

title: Appeal against a result (Kaplan proprietary programmes)
summary: Submit the Appeal Form with detailed reasons within 7 working days of results being released, and pay the appeal fee. Late or incomplete appeals are not accepted.
steps: Get the Appeal Form from Student Services.
Write detailed reasons for your appeal.
Submit it within 7 working days of results release and pay the appeal fee.
notes: University partner programmes follow the university's own appeal rules. Ask your Student Services team.

title: Withdraw, defer or transfer your programme
summary: Tell Kaplan in writing (form, email or letter) with your reasons. Verbal notice is not accepted. You get a written outcome within 4 weeks; keep attending classes until then.
steps: Contact your Student Services team and ask for the withdrawal, deferment or transfer form.
Submit it in writing with your reason. Settle any outstanding fees first.
Under 18? Get your parent or guardian's written consent.
Keep attending classes and stay in contact with Student Services until you receive the written outcome (within 4 weeks).
notes: Deferment: maximum 6 months for Kaplan proprietary programmes; valid reasons include poor academic performance, illness with MC, or compassionate circumstances. International students: deferment or transfer means your Student's Pass is cancelled and must be reapplied for (ICA and Kaplan charges apply). Withdrawing from a single module? University partner programmes have their own rules, so ask Student Services.

title: Enrol in units for next term (Murdoch University)
summary: Your first term's units are enrolled by your programme consultant. For later terms, select units and classes in the Kaplan Student Enrolment Portal about 1.5 to 2 months before the term starts. It is open for 3 to 4 weeks.
steps: Watch for the enrolment portal opening (about 1.5 to 2 months before the new term).
Select your units and classes in the Kaplan Student Enrolment Portal. You can change them while it is open.
After enrolment closes, use the self-check link Kaplan sends you to confirm your classes.
Your valid units will also appear in the Murdoch University student portal.
notes: Kaplan Diploma students who fail a module get a Re-Module App invitation at least a month before term and have 2 weeks to respond.

title: See a doctor using your student medical insurance
summary: Student's Pass holders (and domestic students who opted in) are covered by Kaplan's group medical insurance. You pay a flat $5 to see an Income-affiliated GP.
steps: Find an Income-affiliated GP clinic using the Howden MediHub outpatient manual (linked on the Student Support Services page).
Show your student details at the clinic and pay the $5 co-payment.
For hospital stays, follow the Howden MediHub inpatient manual.
Ask the doctor for an MC if you will miss class, then apply for leave in Kaplan360.
notes: Coverage: up to S$30,000 a year in medical costs, at least a B1 ward in government and restructured hospitals, 24 hours in Singapore (overseas only for school activities, up to 180 days). Domestic opt-in excludes outpatient consultations. Emergency: call 995.

title: Financial help (repayment plans, bursary, loans, scholarships)
summary: Kaplan has a Repayment Assistance Scheme for students in financial difficulty, a Kaplan Bursary for Singaporean and PR students, education loans through banks, and several scholarships.
steps: Repayment Assistance Scheme: apply through your programme consultant with supporting documents.
Kaplan Bursary (Singaporeans and PRs already studying): see the Kaplan Bursary Scheme page.
Education loan: submit your Letter of Offer and Student Contract with the bank's application form (see the bank education loan page).
notes: Unpaid fees lead to Bad Financial Standing: no enrolment, no LMS or Kaplan360 access, no results or graduation. Ask for help early.
contact: Your programme consultant or Student Services

title: Student concession card for buses and MRT
summary: Only Singapore Citizens studying full-time in a degree programme of at least 24 months (or eligible IGCSE students aged 20 and below) qualify. Full-time Diploma students are not eligible.
steps: Eligible students are notified by Kaplan by email. Or ask about eligibility at translink.sg@kaplan.com.
Apply through SimplyGo's PEI Student Concession Card page with a passport photo, NRIC, parent's NRIC and highest qualification certificate.
Processing takes 2 to 4 weeks. Pay $8.10 (Diploma/Degree) when you collect it.
Activate it at a SimplyGo Ticket Office with a minimum $5 top-up.

title: Update your address, phone or email (and tell ICA if on a Student's Pass)
summary: Update your contact details in the Kaplan360 app. Student's Pass holders must also tell ICA within 14 days of changing address or passport.
steps: Open Kaplan360 and update your contact details.
Student's Pass holders: update ICA at ica.gov.sg (Student's Pass, change of local address) within 14 days.
For parent or guardian details, contact Student Services.
notes: If Kaplan can't reach you, you may miss timetable or exam changes.

title: New international student arrival (airport pickup, Reporting Day, accommodation)
summary: New full-time international students get a free airport pickup (submit the form 7 days before arriving), a Reporting Day briefing before orientation, and help with accommodation.
steps: Submit the airport pickup form at least 7 days before you arrive (Changi T1 to T4, Harbourfront, Woodlands). No pickups on public holidays or 11pm to 7am.
Attend Reporting Day for briefings on Student's Pass collection, the medical check-up, your contract, refunds and insurance.
Accommodation: see the Accommodation Services Guide. Kaplan partner hostels and homestays are optional.
Students from China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Malaysia can open an OCBC account before arriving.
notes: There is a 10 calendar day cooling-off period on your contract.

title: Campus locations and opening hours
summary: Kaplan has three city campuses: Wilkie Edge, Odeon 331 and Odeon 333. All open Monday to Friday 9am to 8pm and Saturday 9am to 3pm, and are closed on Sundays and public holidays.
steps: Wilkie Edge: 8 Wilkie Road, Level 2, Singapore 228095 (Level 5 reception opens from 8.15am)
Odeon 331: 331 North Bridge Road, Level 8, Singapore 188720
Odeon 333: 333 North Bridge Road, Level 2, Singapore 188721

title: First aid, fire or safety hazard on campus
summary: For life-threatening situations call 995 immediately. For first aid or safety hazards, call the campus line.
steps: Life-threatening: call 995 (ambulance or fire). Police: 999.
Wilkie Edge: +65 6496 5981
When reporting, say who you are, where (building, level, room), when, and what happened.
notes: During a fire alarm, follow the PA announcements and use the stairs, not the lifts.

title: Support for disabilities or special educational needs
summary: Kaplan can arrange support such as alternative exam arrangements, extra time or help with mobility around campus, based on medical documentation.
steps: Tell Student Services about your needs.
Submit up-to-date medical documentation to Admissions-Assessment and Student Wellbeing & Counselling.
Attend an academic accommodation assessment session to agree on your support.
notes: The support available is subject to university partner policies.

title: Give feedback or make a complaint
summary: Raise the issue with the relevant department or Student Services first. You can also email feedback.sg@kaplan.com at any time. Complaints must include your name and student ID; anonymous complaints are not handled.
steps: Raise it directly with the relevant department or your Student Services team.
Or email feedback.sg@kaplan.com with your full name, student ID, intake code and programme.
Not resolved? Escalate to the Student Services directors listed in the contact list PDF.

title: Join student clubs and activities
summary: Student Engagement and Advancement runs clubs, events and leadership programmes.
steps: Browse clubs on the Kaplan Student Clubs page.
Email sea@kaplan.com to ask about joining or starting a club.
